cultural.vision_reason: The image shows an open-mesh, hand-spun cotton strip-woven cloth with tie-dyed indigo resist patterning, consistent with a Tiv waist-cloth/sash of the type documented by the museum. This matches known Tiv textile traditions of strip-woven, tie-dyed cotton cloths.

physical.title: cloth; waist-cloth
physical.summary: Cloth (an open-mesh sash or waist-cloth), composed of 12 strips of hand-spun cotton sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are identical, each being woven from natural cotton, with the warp threads bunched towards the edges and loosely separated down the middle; the weft is also widely spaced so that the warp and weft together create an open mesh. The cloth after being assembled was tied and dyed in indigo; this has produced a bold pattern of a central circle of undyed cloth with extensions at the four corners, set against an indigo background. The warp ends have been knotted to form a fringe.
